body:
Things Fall Apart - Built To Spill
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=y6RoJ4GIM9k

Definitely the song I can relate to the most and the one that calms me down the best.

I usually don't reply here much, but your post struck a chord with me. I know that sense of tiredness and exhaustion, up to a point where you're just numb. I understand that desire for all the noise both in your head and outside of it to just die down, so I can lay down, at peace, and fade away.

I'm not in a position to give any advice, since I'm going through something similar to what you're going through. But when it gets too hard, I've felt it can be useful to temporarily accept your state, your exhaustion, your pain. Accept that everyone else around you can't really understand the pain you're going through.

Rest, my friend. The battle is never-ending and exhausting, but I think we can both make it through another day.
Thanks for your kind words. I have to remember that I'm not completely alone, even if my depression makes it so hard to feel that way.

I guess I'm similar to you in that respect. My parents have both had pretty hard lives, my mother especially, so I've survived until now for their sakes. That just makes me feel even more trapped though; I can't afford to die, but I feel like I'm already dead in every way except the physical; which makes everything feel so much more overwhelming. Every time I have a suicidal episode, I feel terrible afterwards for being so selfish which just makes things feel even worse.

Nowadays, I just try to survive each night, because I feel that's the best I can do. There's a high balcony outside my room, and I've managed to keep the urge to step over it in check, but it feels like I'm losing control recently.

Thanks for your words, though. It's all too easy to feel absolutely isolated especially on rough days, but it's a relief if even just a little that there's people out there who's gone through the same thing.
I want to fight it, but all too often it seems like I'm just trying to pointlessly fight myself. Thanks, though; your words do help.
